heroHeadline: Somalia Multi-Crisis Day 21: Mogadishu Urban Warfare June 4-5 — Artillery Deployed, Thousands Flee; Turkish F-16 Flyover; 4th Vessel Hijacked Off Garacad; Adan Yabal Day 47
heroSubtitle: On June 3-5, 2026, Somalia's political crisis erupted into the worst urban warfare Mogadishu had seen in more than a decade: a June 3 gunfight at Dabka Junction between government forces and former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire's security detail escalated on June 4 into heavy artillery exchanges across residential neighborhoods — sending thousands of residents fleeing and prompting UN Secretary-General Guterres and the United States to call for immediate restraint. On June 5, the government claimed to have restored order in two districts while Turkish F-16 jets flew low over the capital during mass protests, and Al Jazeera published a major analysis warning Somalia's crisis was deepening. The opposition Somali Future Council's 30-day countdown reached Day 21 with 9 days remaining before Puntland President Said Deni's June 14 deadline for a parallel transitional authority. A fourth cargo vessel was reportedly hijacked off Garacad on June 5 (Al Jazeera) — if confirmed, raising the simultaneous piracy crisis to 4 vessels; the original three vessels remained captive (Honour 25 Day 41/17 crew, Sward Day 40/15 crew, MT Eureka Day 34/12 crew, $10M demand) with all 44 hostages unrescued and no ransom paid. Al-Shabaab held Adan Yabal in Hiiraan for Day 47 — the longest uncontested insurgent town occupation since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive — with no SNA counter-offensive possible as the capital convulsed. Southwest State presidential candidate registration opened June 5 ahead of the contested June 10 vote; the Galmudug/Hirshabelle elections are set for June 20. WFP's July 2026 operational shutdown warning remained active: HRP 15.2% funded; 6.5 million food insecure; 1.84 million children at acute malnutrition risk.
